**Issue #2384 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #2384: Patch: `cargo test` builds the AI optimised, as it already builds the engine and the cards
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The automated tests that play games against the practice AI are among the slowest in the repository. They run the AI's search code with no compiler optimisation, while the game engine and cards it calls into are optimised. Turning optimisation on for the AI too should make those tests several times faster, with no change to any result. Every pull request then waits less for its checks, and the jobs that keep running over time get room.

## Why

- `Cargo.toml:58-83` sets a test opt-level of 2 for `jackioh-engine`, `jackioh-cards`, `jackioh-luau`, `mlua-sys`, `mlua`, `serde_json` and `indexmap`, but not for `jackioh-ai`. `git log -S"profile.test.package.jackioh-ai"` finds no attempt.
- AI-heavy tests are behind the recent over-time fixes:
  - `crates/server/tests/bots/seat.rs:853-857`: "one after another they took most of a minute, the last test `rust (test server)` waited on (#2323)", fixed by threads in #2343.
  - `crates/server/tests/api/practice.rs:233-238`: "each of its AI moves is a full search … held every test thread for over a minute, #2223".
- A job running over time is still an open issue (#2353).

## Proposal

- Add `[profile.test.package.jackioh-ai]` at opt-level 2, or 1 if that measures better once compile time is counted.
- Keep a comment with the measured numbers, as the engine's entry has.
- Debug assertions and overflow checks stay on in the test profile. Rust never reorders floating-point arithmetic at any opt-level, so the AI's decisions and every seeded result are unchanged.

## Where it lands

`Cargo.toml`, and a line in `crates/ai/README.md` if its test notes mention build speed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The PR reports before-and-after wall-clock times, build included, for:
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`;
  - the server's AI-heavy tests (`--test server bots::`, `api::practice`);
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`.
- [ ] Every test passes, with the same outcomes.
- [ ] No `rust (test …)` job on the PR is slower than the same job on `main`.

## Size and risks

A one-entry diff, but real measuring: medium.

- Jobs that build the AI but run little of it pay extra compile time. If those jobs regress, settle on opt-level 1, or drop the change and report the numbers.
- It may help #2353 but does not claim to close it.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

<!-- jackioh-bot -->

```

# Draft plan for #2384 (planner notes)

## Found so far
- `Cargo.toml:58-83`: test-profile opt-level 2 for engine, cards, luau, mlua-sys, mlua, serde_json, indexmap. None for jackioh-ai.
- AI dependents: crates/server, crates/tools, crates/wasm/core (Cargo.toml). Engine/cards/luau don't depend on AI.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` rust-test matrix, cannot be edited by bot): groups that build the AI: server, server api,
  server practice, server practice rulings, ai, ai slow, tools fuzz, tools duos/selfplay, tools wasm. Some groups pass
  `--config profile.test.package.jackioh-engine.opt-level=1` etc. CI env `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`.
- Swatinem/rust-cache: deps cached, workspace crates recompiled every run -> AI compile cost paid every run.
- `crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` builds `--profile test -p jackioh-server --bin jackioh-server --test server_store`: builds AI too
  (db store contract suite; root Cargo.toml does NOT turn db suites on for a PR per scripts/ci-scope.sh:58, but main push runs them).
- Root Cargo.toml change runs every rust group on the PR (scripts/ci-scope.sh:206).
- Internal change: no patch fragment, no player note (docs/issues-and-patches.md).
- crates/ai/README.md Commands section has no build-speed note -> README change optional; plan: none unless...
- AI is pure, no clock: budgets are node counts, so faster code changes no result.

## Shape
One entry in Cargo.toml after `[profile.test.package.jackioh-luau]` with a measured-numbers comment. Builder measures before/after.

## Measurements (planner, this machine: 4 cores, 15 GB)
Script: /tmp/measure2384/measure.sh <ai-opt> <group...> (mirrors ci.yml groups 1-9 + 10 = db store build;
env CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; `cargo clean -p <every workspace member>` first; build via --no-run, then run).
Uses `--config profile.test.package.jackioh-ai.opt-level=L` so no edit needed. Results in /tmp/measure2384/results.tsv.
Warm build of all groups' deps: ~625 s.
(running L=0 vs L=2 for all groups)

## Decisions
- No README change: crates/ai/README.md Commands section says nothing about build speed.
- No new test: a profile setting has no behaviour to test; the proof is the whole suite passing with identical `test result:` lines and the timings.
- floats: AI uses sqrt (exact), exp (libm call, non-const arg), powf(x, 20.0) in shadow_ban::shaped_weight (LLVM may rewrite pow with const exponent? Suite decides).
- Can't touch .github/ci.yml: per-group `--config profile.test.package.jackioh-ai.opt-level=0` for groups running no AI is a person's follow-up.
